decisions: The acceptance page is also a Guide entry ('Your First Evening with 1.0'), so the owner can read the next step on the evening; it obeys the on-screen rules (no key named, Apps, Kasandra). It is NOT yet in name_sweep.GUIDE_PAGES because the coordinator's own marker '<!-- COORDINATOR: fill after F2 merges -->' contains 'F2', which the key pattern reads as a function key; everything else on the page passes in_guides.

Each coordinator block opens with the asked marker and closes with '<!-- /COORDINATOR -->'. F2's block is in docs/ACCEPTANCE_1.0.md (Part 1: the 0.8.7 workspace, the cold start, stalls); M2's are in docs/ACCEPTANCE_1.0.md (Part 3.2) and docs/GUIDE_KASANDRA.md (Her model). Qt's Markdown reader does not show the comments (checked); the viewer's Text page shows the source.
The guide pages' data live in a module of their own (workbench/guide_pages.py: PAGES and actions()); menus2 gets three keys in HELP and a four-line block after K6's, both marked 1.0 X2.

Rail Demo has no long specification, .odt report or worksheet: in the section 18 day its limits sheet (Rev B, CURRENT) plays the specification, the bench readings sheet the worksheet and 'Rail Demo summary' the report; the change is the demo's own (settled current 250 to 300 mA). Where it is not known that the behaviour is built (whether she notices the stale summary by herself), the page asks the owner to write down what happened and gives the words to ask her if she did not.

Closing and returning (section 18's 'when you return') reopens the same Rail Demo folder with one Terminal line that sets exactly what Try Rail Demo sets for its window (demo_try.demo_environment) and drops ARC_LEDGER_EDITION as it does, detached with setsid -f; it does not start with 'cd ' because Graphite's Terminal treats such a line as its own cd. The line was run in the smoke with a stand-in python.

The crash test in Part 2 (Graphite comes back, apps stay) uses 'pkill --oldest --signal KILL --full workbench.launch' from Graphite's own Terminal: --oldest picks the session's window, not the shell running the command nor a demo window started later.
The model check's tuning box is 240 s by default; the page offers a console rerun with --tuning-seconds 900 only if the card says the box ran out (each tuning row is a fresh launch of a 22 GB model).

What to send back: the photos, the model check's two for-sending files (privacy-scanned), ~/.local/state/ledger-slate/{session.log,last-session.json,launch-error.log} (to be looked at first: launch-error.log can name home folders), and the Rail Demo folder as a tar (invented data; paths may carry the account name). Never the workspace, the profile or a backup.

release_note: The Guide for 1.0: Guide ▸ The Living Desktop (the whole desktop on one screen: the session and the dock, Apps, Files from This computer, DELETE, the Machine, the board and its wires, opening and working, tabs and the split, the foot's line, HALT, the looks) and Guide ▸ Kasandra, the Ghost in the Shell (her column, how she does a task under your grants and verifies it, her journal, her hand in your apps and how a touch stops her, the sealed utility, the network, what she never does, her model and its check). Guide ▸ Your First Evening with 1.0 (docs/ACCEPTANCE_1.0.md) is the acceptance evening on the ThinkPad: the install from the kit, your paper's test with no model, her 35B and the model check's tuning, the day on Rail Demo, and what to send back. Getting Started and the ThinkPad page are brought up to 1.0. Built, not tested: the first real proof is that evening.
